name: Analytical Path
description: Designed for engineers, data scientists, analysts, and technical professionals

lessons.title: Welcome to Analytical Prompting
lessons.content: Precision is everything. In analytical work, vague prompts lead to unreliable outputs. This course teaches you to craft prompts with the same rigor you apply to your code and analysis.
keyPoints: Define inputs, outputs, and constraints explicitly

lessons.title: Exercise 1: SQL Query Generation
lessons.scenario: You have a database with tables: users (id, email, signup_date), orders (id, user_id, amount, order_date), and products (id, name, category). You need complex queries for analysis.
lessons.task: Write a prompt that generates a SQL query to find the top 10 customers by total spend in Q4 2024, including their signup dates and order counts.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: schema reference, explicit column names, date range specification, aggregation logic, result format
hints: Reference the exact table and column names
Specify date range format (YYYY-MM-DD)
Define what 'top 10' means (by total spend)
List all columns needed in output
Specify ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Constraints & Edge Cases
lessons.content: Analytical work requires thinking about edge cases. Your prompts should define boundaries, handle nulls, and specify what to do with outliers.

examples.better: Analyze this dataset: calculate mean and median. Handle null values by excluding them. Flag outliers >3 standard deviations. Return results in JSON format with 2 decimal precision.

lessons.title: Exercise 2: Data Cleaning Specification
lessons.scenario: You have a messy CSV with customer data: inconsistent date formats, mixed case names, phone numbers in various formats, duplicate emails, and null values.
lessons.task: Write a prompt that specifies exactly how to clean this data, handling each issue with explicit rules.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: explicit handling of each data quality issue, edge case coverage, output format specification, validation rules
hints: List every data quality issue explicitly
Define handling rules for each (standardize, remove, flag?)
Specify output format for each field
Define validation rules
Explain how to handle edge cases (e.g., duplicate emails with different names)

lessons.title: Exercise 3: Statistical Analysis
lessons.scenario: You have A/B test results: Variant A (5,000 users, 250 conversions) vs Variant B (5,000 users, 290 conversions). Determine statistical significance and provide business recommendation.
lessons.task: Write a prompt that requests proper statistical analysis with specific tests, confidence levels, and interpretation.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: correct test specification, confidence level, p-value interpretation, practical significance, business recommendation format
hints: Specify the statistical test (two-proportion z-test)
Request confidence level (95%, 99%?)
Ask for p-value AND effect size
Define minimum detectable effect that matters to business
Request both statistical AND practical significance
Specify output format for recommendation

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Structured Output
lessons.content: Analytical outputs need structure. Always specify the exact format you need: JSON schema, table structure, or report template.

examples.unstructured: Give me insights from this data
examples.structured: Analyze this data and return JSON: {"summary": {"total_records": int, "date_range": str}, "top_insights": [{"category": str, "metric": str, "value": float, "change_pct": float}], "anomalies": [{"date": str, "issue": str, "severity": str}]}

lessons.title: Exercise 4: API Documentation
lessons.scenario: You need to document a REST API endpoint that creates user accounts. The endpoint has complex validation rules, error responses, and rate limiting.
lessons.task: Write a prompt that generates comprehensive API documentation with all technical details, examples, and edge cases.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: completeness of technical details, example requests/responses, error documentation, edge case coverage
hints: Specify documentation structure (endpoint, method, parameters, responses)
Request example curl commands
List all possible error codes and meanings
Include rate limiting details
Request parameter validation rules with types
Ask for edge case examples

lessons.title: Exercise 5: Algorithm Explanation
lessons.scenario: Explain how the PageRank algorithm works to different audiences: 1) junior developers, 2) non-technical stakeholders, 3) technical interview setting.
lessons.task: Write a prompt that generates three different explanations of the same algorithm, each tailored to audience technical level and context.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: technical accuracy, audience-appropriate language, completeness for each context, example usage
hints: Specify exactly what each audience needs to know
Define technical depth for each (formula? pseudocode? analogy?)
Request different examples for each audience
Specify length constraints for each version
Ask for diagrams or visual aid descriptions

lessons.title: Final Challenge: Full Data Analysis Report
lessons.scenario: Analyze e-commerce data to identify why conversion rates dropped 15% last quarter. Data includes: user behavior (5M records), product catalog (10K SKUs), marketing spend by channel, competitor pricing, site performance metrics.
lessons.task: Write a comprehensive prompt that specifies a complete analytical investigation including data exploration, hypothesis testing, root cause analysis, and actionable recommendations.
lessons.evaluationCriteria: analytical rigor, hypothesis structure, data requirements specification, statistical methods, output format, actionability
hints: Define the analytical framework (what questions to answer)
Specify which datasets to analyze and how
Request specific statistical tests for each hypothesis
Define output structure (executive summary, methodology, findings, recommendations)
Specify visualization requirements
Request confidence levels for all claims
Ask for sensitivity analysis
Define how to prioritize recommendations
